context.situation: You've been invited to an online interview for a project coordinator role at an international NGO. The interviewer starts with the classic questions.
context.situation_ar: دُعيت إلى مقابلة عبر الإنترنت لوظيفة منسق مشاريع في منظمة دولية. تبدأ المقابِلة بالأسئلة المعتادة.
context.goal: Talk about your experience, responsibilities and strengths, and give examples under pressure.
context.goal_ar: أن تتحدث عن خبرتك ومسؤولياتك ونقاط قوتك، وتعطي أمثلة تحت الضغط.

script.t: Thanks for joining us, Zainab. Could you start by telling me a bit about yourself?
Of course. I've been working in project coordination for about four years, mainly with education projects in Erbil and Duhok.
And what are you responsible for in your current role?
I'm responsible for planning activities with our partners, managing a budget of around two hundred thousand dollars, and reporting to donors.
What would you say is your main strength?
I'd say I'm good at dealing with people who disagree. I've learnt to listen first and find what both sides actually need.
Can you tell me about a difficult decision you had to make?

Sure. Last year, a partner school couldn't deliver on time, and we had to decide whether to cancel the workshop or move it online. I spoke to the teachers, weighed up the risks, and we moved it online. Attendance actually went up.
Impressive. And how do you handle working under pressure?
I break big deadlines into small steps, and I tell my manager early if something's going wrong, rather than at the last minute.
Great. Do you have any questions for us?
Yes — what would success look like in the first six months? I'm really looking forward to hearing more about the team.

gist.prompt: What impression does Zainab give overall?
options: Experienced, calm, and able to give concrete examples

detail.prompt: How long has Zainab been working in project coordination?

Because she doesn't understand the job

notice.quote: I've been working in project coordination for about four years.

question.prompt: Is Zainab still working in project coordination?
options: Yes — it started in the past and continues now.
No, she stopped four years ago.

notice.explain: have been + -ing + for/since: an activity that started in the past and is still going on.
notice.explain_ar: have been + ing + for/since: نشاط بدأ في الماضي ومستمر حتى الآن.

notice.quote: I'm really looking forward to hearing more about the team.

options: Because "to" here is a preposition, so an -ing form follows.

notice.explain: look forward to + -ing (looking forward to meeting you). The "to" is a preposition, not part of an infinitive.
notice.explain_ar: بعد look forward to يأتي الفعل مع ing.

grammar.title: Present perfect continuous for experience that continues
grammar.context: I've been working in project coordination for about four years.
grammar.pattern: have / has + been + verb-ing + for (length) / since (start)
examples: She's been managing the team for two years.
How long have you been working there?
We've been planning this project for months.
grammar.explain: Use it to say how long an ongoing activity has lasted. Use for with a length of time and since with a starting point.
grammar.explain_ar: للتعبير عن مدة نشاط مستمر. for مع المدة و since مع البداية.

errors.why: Since 2021 → it started then and continues: have been working.
errors.why_ar: since 2021 ← بدأ ومستمر: have been working.

practice.sentence: I'm working here since three years.
answers: I've been working here for three years.
I have been working here for three years.
practice.why: Ongoing duration → have been working; three years is a length → for.
practice.why_ar: مدة مستمرة ← have been working، والمدة ← for.

practice.text: In my current job I'm responsible ___ training new staff.

errors.why: The preposition is for: responsible for.

practice.sentence: I look forward to meet you.
answers: I look forward to meeting you.
I'm looking forward to meeting you.
I am looking forward to meeting you.
practice.why: After look forward to we use -ing: meeting.

free.instruction: Answer the interviewer: "Tell me about yourself." (about one minute)

turns.say: Thanks for joining us. Could you start by telling me a bit about yourself?

expect.reply: Thank you. What would you say is your main strength?

fallback.reply: Just a brief summary of your background is fine.
fallback.hint: Try: I've been working as … for … years.

turns.model: Sure. I've been working as a teacher for three years, and before that I studied English literature.

expect.reply: Could you give me an example of that?

fallback.reply: What are you particularly good at?
fallback.hint: Try: I'd say I'm good at…

expect.reply: Good. Now, tell me about a difficult decision you had to make.

fallback.hint: Try: For example, last year I…

turns.model: For example, last year I organised a conference for two hundred people.

expect.reply: Thank you, that's very helpful. Do you have any questions for us?

fallback.reply: What was the decision, and what happened?
fallback.hint: Try: I had to decide whether to… In the end,…

turns.model: I had to decide whether to cancel an event or move it online. In the end, we moved it online.

expect.reply: Good question. We'd expect you to know all our partners and run your first project review. We'll be in touch next week.
OK. We'll be in touch next week.

fallback.reply: Anything you'd like to know about the role?
fallback.hint: Try: What would success look like in the first six months?

turns.model: Yes — what would success look like in the first six months?

fallback.hint: Try: Thank you. I look forward to hearing from you.

turns.model: Thank you for your time. I look forward to hearing from you.
